blocks.x: Predictive Maintenance & Asset Intelligence as delivered by Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, the platforms involved and the outcomes we commit to at each gate.

Predictive maintenance pays when it changes the plan: remaining-useful-life models feeding scheduler decisions, spare-parts availability and maintenance-window selection. We build the full loop — governed telemetry from the sensor network, failure-mode-driven model design (not generic anomaly detection), RUL and condition models validated against work-order history, and integration into EAM/CMMS (SAP PM/Maximo-class) so predictions become scheduled work with parts reserved, not dashboard decorations.

We start where physics pays: rotating equipment, transformers, compressors, conveyors, fleet drivetrains — failure modes with measurable precursors. Clients see the outcome in planning language: unplanned downtime hours, maintenance cost per unit of output, planner trust (the share of predictions acted upon). False-alarm discipline is a first-class design goal; one crying-wolf quarter kills the program politically.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
